author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected afterwards, held to the same rules as the original booking, amending the existing visit rather than leaving the pet with a second one.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when it is opened for correction, then that visit's booked date and description are offered as the values to change
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are supplied, then that visit carries the new date and description and the correction is confirmed
given a pet with one booked visit, when a correction to it is accepted, then the pet still has exactly one visit
given a booked visit, when a blank description is submitted, then the correction is refused and the description is named
given a booked visit, when a date of today or earlier is submitted, then the correction is refused and the date is named
given a refused correction, when the reader is shown the form again, then the visit as booked is unchanged
given a pet that does not belong to the named owner, when a correction to one of its visits is attempted, then it is refused
non_goals: cancelling or deleting a booked visit - NG-5 as narrowed, and NG-4
changing anything about a visit other than its date and description
moving a visit to a different pet or owner
notes: NG-5 narrowed on 2026-08-04 from 'Changing or cancelling a visit once booked' to 'Cancelling a visit once booked'. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-04-non-goal-visit-amendment.md, authored here: docs/adr/README.md section 'Non-Goal ADRs' assigns non-goal ADRs to product-requirements-expert, not system-design-expert. Two follow-ups outside this agent's write scope: (1) the ADR index table in docs/adr/README.md needs a row for the new ADR; (2) system-design-expert owns that edit. Open and deliberately unrequired: whether the owner detail page gains a link to the correction form, and whether the correction form shows the pet's other visits as REQ-VIS-002 requires of the booking form. Validation rules for the correction are REQ-VIS-001's, unchanged.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the create-or-update controller shape the owner feature already demonstrates, applied to a third entity. No new package, no new pattern, no new dependency, no ADR: PetController already pairs a /new route with a /{id}/edit route on one controller, resolves the entity in a @ModelAttribute loader that takes the id as a required=false @PathVariable, reuses one createOrUpdate template, and redirects to the owner detail page. VisitController adopts the same shape. The one real adjustment is that VisitController's existing @ModelAttribute("visit") loader unconditionally does `new Visit()` + `pet.addVisit(visit)` for every handler in the controller (VisitController.java:63-81), which on a correction route would leave the pet with a second visit on save and would offer tomorrow's default date instead of the booked one. The loader therefore gains a `@PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId` parameter: null keeps today's booking behavior exactly as-is, non-null resolves the existing Visit by traversing the loaded pet's visits and returns it without addVisit. Aggregate traversal stays in the model as a new `Pet.getVisit(Integer id)` mirroring `Owner.getPet(Integer id)`, which preserves the invariant recorded in docs/system-design.md Contracts that Owner is the aggregate entry point and Pet and Visit are reached and persisted only through it. Persistence needs nothing new: the loader puts the same Owner instance into the model that the Visit was taken from, so form binding mutates the Visit in place inside owner.getPet(petId).getVisits() and the existing this.owners.save(owner) cascades an UPDATE rather than an INSERT.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit added to VisitController, both rendering the existing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm view and the POST redirecting to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} on success
VisitController's shared @ModelAttribute("visit") loader becomes route-aware via a required=false visitId path variable; the booking route's behavior must be unchanged
Pet gains getVisit(Integer id) as the aggregate traversal accessor; no repository for Visit is introduced
pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its visit model attribute are reused unchanged - no template edit, no new message key

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute loader taking the entity id as required=false @PathVariable so one loader serves both the create and the edit route - the shape the visit loader adopts
the /new plus /{id}/edit route pair on one controller, sharing one createOrUpdate view and redirecting to the owner detail page
getPet(Integer id) - traversal by identity within the aggregate, returning null when absent; Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirrors it
the non-future date rejection (result.rejectValue with typeMismatch.visitDate) that the correction path reuses verbatim alongside @Valid for the @NotBlank description

risks.risk: The shared @ModelAttribute("visit") loader runs before every handler in VisitController and today creates and adds a Visit. Reused unmodified on the correction route it produces exactly the failure the ADR names: save cascades an INSERT and the pet ends up with two visits.
risks.mitigation: Branch the loader on the required=false visitId: only the null branch does new Visit() + pet.addVisit(visit). Cover it with the prd-entry's theVisitCorrectionShouldAmendTheVisitWithoutAddingAnother, asserting the pet's visit count and the corrected field values on the saved Owner.

risks.risk: If the correction handler resolves the Owner independently of the loader (a second owners.findById, as PetController.findPet does), the bound Visit belongs to a different object graph than the saved Owner and the correction silently persists nothing while still redirecting with a success message.
risks.mitigation: Keep the loader's single findById and take the Owner from the model (@ModelAttribute Owner owner, as processNewVisitForm already does). If a copy-onto-the-existing-entity step feels needed as in PetController.updatePetDetails, that is the signal the graphs have diverged - consult rather than adding the copy.

risks.risk: Form binding mutates the in-graph Visit before validation runs, so the acceptance criterion that a refused correction leaves the visit unchanged rests entirely on the error path never persisting.
risks.mitigation: Return the form view before any save call, and do not put @Transactional on the handler. The graph is detached (spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled - docs/system-design.md Persistence), so an unsaved mutation is never dirty-checked to the database.

risks.risk: The previous-visits table in createOrUpdateVisitForm filters rows with th:if="${!visit['new']}" against the loop variable; that filter is what hides the blank booking-path visit and is load-bearing for REQ-VIS-002.
risks.mitigation: Do not touch the template. On the correction path every visit in the set is persisted, so all of them render, including the one under correction - see notes.

risks.risk: The visitId is a nested path variable arriving from an unauthenticated caller (docs/system-design.md Security Context: no authentication, authorization, or CSRF anywhere), so a guessed id must not reach another pet's visit.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only by traversing the already-ownership-checked pet's visits, never by a global lookup by id. Absence fails closed with the same IllegalArgumentException shape as the existing pet guard, which makes cross-pet and cross-owner access structurally impossible rather than checked.

risks.risk: Any new user-facing string costs eleven message bundles; I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails both on a key missing from one locale and on a template literal not covered by th:text.
risks.mitigation: This slice adds no message key. The heading already degrades from "New Visit" to "Visit" via visit['new'], and the submit button keeps #{addVisit}. If the implementer believes new wording is needed, that is a product question - stop and consult, do not add a key.

Adding one is new user-facing text on a page that serves REQ-OWN-003, needs a new message key in all eleven bundles, and is covered by no acceptance criterion and no test name in this prd-entry. Recommend a follow-up requirement rather than folding it in here - the implementer must not invent the link in this slice. Vocabulary tension, pre-existing and non-blocking: docs/ubiquitous-language.md lists Booking under Avoid for Visit, while docs/prd.md REQ-VIS-001 and REQ-VIS-003 use "booking" and "booked" throughout. author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: loadPetWithVisit's branch on visitId is documented with an updated javadoc that states both the booking and correction contracts and the ownership-safety rationale (traversal-only lookup, no global-by-id lookup)

Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer id) exactly in shape, null-return contract, and javadoc wording (verified against Owner.java:113-127) - a faithful, low-surprise extension of the existing aggregate-traversal idiom

The duplicated non-future-date check between processNewVisitForm and processUpdateVisitForm mirrors PetController's own duplicated birth-date check (verified at PetController.java:116-117 and :159-160, identical shape); given the codebase's established precedent for this exact duplication, not extracting it here keeps VisitController consistent with its sibling controller rather than introducing a one-off abstraction

Error messages for the new visit-not-found case follow the existing pet-not-found message's exact phrasing and field order

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Object-reference authorization verified as claimed: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit (VisitController.java:69-96) resolves the owner by id, then reaches the pet only via owner.getPet(petId) and the visit only via pet.getVisit(visitId). Both traversals are in-aggregate, so a mismatched-but-existing ownerId/petId/visitId combination cannot reach another owner's or another pet's data - the loader throws IllegalArgumentException before any handler runs. There is no repository lookup by visit id and no VisitRepository, so no global-id path exists. Confirmed by reading Pet.getVisit: it iterates only this pet's visits, skips unsaved ones (isNew()), and compares with Objects.equals, so a null or unmatched id fails closed with null rather than matching by accident.

Mass assignment: the correction POST binds two model attributes, and neither is over-permissive in a new way. Visit carries only date and description as bindable properties (Visit.java) - no pet back-reference and no owner reference exist on the entity, so a client cannot re-point a visit to another pet or owner through form binding. The id is blocked by the controller's existing @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") (VisitController.java:51-54), which applies to every handler in the controller and therefore covers both new routes; the "*.id" pattern also covers the nested pets[n].id and pets[n].visits[n].id paths reachable through the Owner attribute. The @ModelAttribute Owner binding on the correction handler is byte-for-byte the same posture the pre-existing booking handler (processNewVisitForm) already carries, so the new route introduces no new bindable surface.

Persistence on the refusal path verified end to end: processUpdateVisitForm has no @Transactional, returns the form view before any owners.save call, and spring.jpa.open-in-view=false is confirmed present in src/main/resources/application.properties:11 (the design's assumption holds, and it is the only occurrence in the repository). The Owner graph handed to the handler comes from owners.findById outside any handler-scoped transaction and is therefore detached, so the in-memory mutation binding applied to the visit is never dirty-checked to the database. The refusal path leaves the booked visit unchanged in storage.

Output escaping: no template changed, and src/main/resources/templates/pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html contains no th:utext - the reused form renders the visit description through Thymeleaf's default-escaping th:text/th:field, so a stored description cannot become stored XSS on the new correction surface.
Error handling leaks nothing new: the IllegalArgumentException message echoes only the ids the caller itself supplied, matching the shape of the pre-existing pet guard on the same loader.

No secrets in the diff: swept the change set for credential-shaped material (token, password, secret, key, and the datasource-credential names the project's security brief flags) - no hits in any changed file.

Supply chain: the change set touches no build file (build.gradle, pom.xml, gradle/, settings.gradle are all unmodified), so no dependency is added, removed, or version-shifted and the Spring Boot 4.1.0 baseline is unchanged by this slice. No dependencyCheck plugin is configured in build.gradle, so no CVE scan is wired into the build; that is a pre-existing project-level gap, not something this change alters.

Threat-model baseline respected: the change adds a second mutating POST surface under the recorded NG-1 posture (no authentication, authorization, or CSRF anywhere - docs/system-design.md Security Context). It introduces no new class of exposure beyond that recorded baseline, and per the standing project context the absent access-control layer is not re-reported here.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Both refusal tests express the 'a refused correction leaves the visit as booked unchanged' acceptance criterion solely via verify(owners, never()).save(any(Owner.class)). That is an accurate proxy for durable state (no save call means the DB row is untouched), but it is silent about a real subtlety the design-block itself flags: WebDataBinder mutates the in-graph Visit (this.bookedVisit, the same instance pet.getVisit(visitId) returns) before validation runs. After either POST, this.bookedVisit.getDescription()/getDate() actually hold the invalid submitted values, not BOOKED_DESCRIPTION/BOOKED_DATE - the tests never assert this either way. A reader relying on the test name and the never(save) call alone could reasonably believe the booked Visit object itself was left untouched, which is false; a future contributor 'strengthening' the test by naively asserting bookedVisit.getDescription() equals BOOKED_DESCRIPTION after a refusal would hit a red herring: the resulting failure is not a regression, it is confirming the (correct, intentional) in-place binding behavior the design-block already reasoned about.
findings.fix: In both refusal tests, add one explicit assertion (with a short comment) that documents the in-place mutation, e.g. `assertThat(this.bookedVisit.getDescription()).isEmpty(); // binding mutates the in-graph visit before validation; only the missing save() below keeps this from persisting`, and correspondingly for the date test. This converts the currently-implicit assumption into a locked-in, documented specification of exactly what 'unchanged' means at this test level (persisted state, not object state), so the never(save) assertion is no longer the only signal of the property and a reader is not misled about what is and is not preserved.

findings.description: hasMessageContaining("Visit with id 99 not found for pet with id 1.") hard-codes the pet id as a bare literal '1' that happens to match TEST_PET_ID by coincidence rather than by reference - a Tier 3 mystery literal per the three-tier data naming convention. If TEST_PET_ID is ever changed, this assertion silently stops matching the real message text instead of failing loudly or updating with it.
findings.fix: Build the expected fragment from the existing constants, e.g. `.hasMessageContaining("Visit with id " + visitOfAnotherPet + " not found for pet with id " + TEST_PET_ID)`.

title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected afterwards, held to the same rules as the original booking, amending the existing visit rather than leaving the pet with a second one.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when it is opened for correction, then that visit's booked date and description are offered as the values to change
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are supplied, then that visit carries the new date and description and the correction is confirmed
given a pet with one booked visit, when a correction to it is accepted, then the pet still has exactly one visit
given a booked visit, when a blank description is submitted, then the correction is refused and the description is named
given a booked visit, when a date of today or earlier is submitted, then the correction is refused and the date is named
given a refused correction, when the reader is shown the form again, then the visit as booked is unchanged
given a pet that does not belong to the named owner, when a correction to one of its visits is attempted, then it is refused
non_goals: cancelling or deleting a booked visit - NG-5 as narrowed, and NG-4
changing anything about a visit other than its date and description
moving a visit to a different pet or owner

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Unchanged from the superseded records at lines 4 and 9. Visit correction is the create-or-update controller shape the owner feature already demonstrates, applied to a third entity. No new package, no new pattern, no new dependency, no ADR: PetController already pairs a /new route with a /{id}/edit route on one controller, resolves the entity in a @ModelAttribute loader that takes the id as a required=false @PathVariable, reuses one createOrUpdate template, and redirects to the owner detail page. VisitController adopts the same shape. The one real adjustment is that VisitController's existing @ModelAttribute("visit") loader unconditionally does `new Visit()` + `pet.addVisit(visit)` for every handler in the controller (VisitController.java:63-81), which on a correction route would leave the pet with a second visit on save and would offer tomorrow's default date instead of the booked one. The loader therefore gains a `@PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId` parameter: null keeps today's booking behavior exactly as-is, non-null resolves the existing Visit by traversing the loaded pet's visits and returns it without addVisit. Aggregate traversal stays in the model as a new `Pet.getVisit(Integer id)` mirroring `Owner.getPet(Integer id)`, which preserves the invariant recorded in docs/system-design.md Contracts that Owner is the aggregate entry point and Pet and Visit are reached and persisted only through it. Persistence needs nothing new: the loader puts the same Owner instance into the model that the Visit was taken from, so form binding mutates the Visit in place inside owner.getPet(petId).getVisits() and the existing this.owners.save(owner) cascades an UPDATE rather than an INSERT.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit added to VisitController, both rendering the existing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm view and the POST redirecting to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} on success
VisitController's shared @ModelAttribute("visit") loader becomes route-aware via a required=false visitId path variable; the booking route's behavior must be unchanged

pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its visit model attribute are reused unchanged - no template edit, no new message key

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute loader taking the entity id as required=false @PathVariable so one loader serves both the create and the edit route - the shape the visit loader adopts
the /new plus /{id}/edit route pair on one controller, sharing one createOrUpdate view and redirecting to the owner detail page
getPet(Integer id) - traversal by identity within the aggregate, returning null when absent; Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirrors it
the non-future date rejection (result.rejectValue with typeMismatch.visitDate) that the correction path reuses verbatim alongside @Valid for the @NotBlank description

risks.risk: The shared @ModelAttribute("visit") loader runs before every handler in VisitController and today creates and adds a Visit. Reused unmodified on the correction route it produces exactly the failure the ADR names: save cascades an INSERT and the pet ends up with two visits.
risks.mitigation: Branch the loader on the required=false visitId: only the null branch does new Visit() + pet.addVisit(visit). Cover it with the prd-entry's theVisitCorrectionShouldAmendTheVisitWithoutAddingAnother, asserting the pet's visit count and the corrected field values on the saved Owner.

risks.risk: If the correction handler resolves the Owner independently of the loader (a second owners.findById, as PetController.findPet does), the bound Visit belongs to a different object graph than the saved Owner and the correction silently persists nothing while still redirecting with a success message.
risks.mitigation: Keep the loader's single findById and take the Owner from the model (@ModelAttribute Owner owner, as processNewVisitForm already does). If a copy-onto-the-existing-entity step feels needed as in PetController.updatePetDetails, that is the signal the graphs have diverged - consult rather than adding the copy.

risks.risk: Form binding mutates the in-graph Visit before validation runs, so the acceptance criterion that a refused correction leaves the visit unchanged rests entirely on the error path never persisting.
risks.mitigation: Return the form view before any save call, and do not put @Transactional on the handler. The graph is detached (spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled - docs/system-design.md Persistence), so an unsaved mutation is never dirty-checked to the database.

risks.risk: The previous-visits table in createOrUpdateVisitForm filters rows with th:if="${!visit['new']}" against the loop variable; that filter is what hides the blank booking-path visit and is load-bearing for REQ-VIS-002.
risks.mitigation: Do not touch the template. On the correction path every visit in the set is persisted, so all of them render, including the one under correction - see notes.

risks.risk: The visitId is a nested path variable arriving from an unauthenticated caller (docs/system-design.md Security Context: no authentication, authorization, or CSRF anywhere), so a guessed id must not reach another pet's visit.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only by traversing the already-ownership-checked pet's visits, never by a global lookup by id. Absence fails closed with the same IllegalArgumentException shape as the existing pet guard, which makes cross-pet and cross-owner access structurally impossible rather than checked.

risks.risk: Any new user-facing string costs eleven message bundles; I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails both on a key missing from one locale and on a template literal not covered by th:text.
risks.mitigation: This slice adds no message key. The heading already degrades from "New Visit" to "Visit" via visit['new'], and the submit button keeps #{addVisit}. If the implementer believes new wording is needed, that is a product question - stop and consult, do not add a key.
